sections.title: Numbers and Prices
sections.content: Here are the numbers you need to shop with. You will meet the whole system, and the clock, in Lesson 12 — for now, enough to read a label and understand a total. To ask a price, Spanish makes the thing the subject: 'cuesta' for one item, 'cuestan' for several. So it is '¿cuánto cuesta el pan?' but '¿cuánto cuestan los tomates?'.

sections.title: Numbers
rows: cero, uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco

items.spanish: Treinta y cinco mil dongs el kilo.

items.english: That's six hundred and twenty thousand dong.

items.spanish: Carlos paga con su tarjeta en la caja.
items.english: Carlos pays by card at the checkout.

sections.content: From 16 to 29 the number is written as one word — dieciséis, veintiuno — and from 31 up it splits again with 'y': treinta y cinco, cuarenta y dos.
